counts.meaning: diagnostic frames, not 320 public editing correctness cases

findings.cost: M with endpoint/UI regression policy; radius-only edit is small but insufficient
facts: Qt uses floor input and QRect(start,end).normalized, drawRoundedRect(...,12,12), default aliased drawing. Studio retains float min/abs, scalar min(14,w/2,h/2) and Canvas vector AA.
wide-short uses independently limited Qt x/y radii. Actual Canvas scalar12 remains byte-equal to current14 in this short-height case; axis12 changes 68 pixels, including one opaque255↔zero conflict.
Qt positive QRect [8,8,65,41] versus reverse [9,9,63,39]; Studio both directions [8,8,64,40]. Qt point/line dimensions and floor rules also differ.
findings.interpretation: Radius, endpoint extent/direction, degenerate geometry, AA/cap/join are distinct decisions. Confirmed parity gaps do not by themselves establish data loss or require copying a legacy direction quirk.

facts: Original reused default Canvas produced different raw edge pixels for equivalent large/reverse geometry.

A separate controlled followup used willReadFrequently:true versus fresh default Canvas, repeated each geometry 3 times with order swap. Within each context condition identical geometry was byte-stable and before/after Canvas state/Studio fields agreed.

Between fixed readback and fresh default, fill differed101 pixels/maxAlpha89; outline1 differed252/maxAlpha126. Opaque255↔zero conflicts were0. Original first/late outputs matched the corresponding controlled contexts.
findings.interpretation: This supports a context/readback condition association. No internal GPU/backend transition was directly observed; no product tile/preview defect, performance or global willReadFrequently change is inferred.

decision.reason: Bare14→12 does not restore Qt geometry. Axis12 with Studio bounds preserves other Studio tools endpoints but is not full Qt parity; fullQtBounds changes direction/point geometry and still differs in aliased raster. No partial candidate is applied before the endpoint and public UI contracts are fixed.

options.name: Studio endpoints + independently clamped max12 radii
options.scope: Only roundrect path changes; float/min/abs and consistent rectangle/ellipse endpoints remain
options.remaining: Explicit corner policy, actual public preview/commit/Undo/cancel/512 seam/DPR validation; does not claim strict Qt endpoints

options.name: strict Qt endpoint policy
options.scope: Evaluate rectangle/ellipse/roundrect together, with floor, reverse, point/line, Shift and bbox changes
options.remaining: Risk to current UI consistency, AA/cap/join and raw raster remain separate; cannot silently apply global min/abs+1

next: Use stable context conditions and actual public UI prototypes to compare preview, pending project export and final raster.
Choose one documented endpoint/corner policy consistent across rectangle/ellipse/roundrect, preserve saved project pixels.
Before adoption verify point/line/reverse/fractional/negative clip, outline/fill/alpha, one Undo/Redo/cancel, 512 seams and DPR1/2.

limits: Qt QPainter aliased versus Canvas vector antialiasing are different raster contracts; raw differences alone do not prove a pixel bug
No Qt runtime rerun, no app/public UI/native/device test, no performance claims
Strict opaque/transparent observed conflict is descriptive; geometric full-cell proof is used only where original QtPath annotations provide it
Canvas cell annotations use existing original geometry evidence; empty annotation lists are not proof that no other geometric differences exist

Original first two current14 large style samples and later variants did not share a demonstrated fixed raster condition; retain them as default-context observations, not a clean causal scalar14-vs12 A/B.
Only narrow current14 same-geometry followup controls were rerun; other variants were not all rerun in both fixed modes.
NewDOMPoint instance construction was not used; the supported radii object is DOMPointInit.
No color/opacity/IME/gesture pressure or OS display/device acceptance; no Qt actualCanvas UI run here.
